FIND: C0009 is confirmed. In `build_feedback_sections`, the docstring promises `max_chars_per_model` is a hard cap, but the fallback placeholder can exceed the cap when `max_chars_per_model` is smaller than the placeholder length. Premises: (1) the loop exits immediately after assigning the placeholder; (2) no final clamp is applied before `sections[model_id] = section`; (3) callers can pass small or zero budgets. Concrete trace: with one feedback record and `max_chars_per_model=10`, the loop drops all `top_items`, assigns a multi-line placeholder longer than 10 characters, breaks, and stores it. Expected: `len(sections[model_id]) <= 10`. Actual: returned section length is greater than 10.

FOLLOW: Downstream prompt assembly may rely on this function as the last budget guard. If it returns text longer than the stated hard cap, later assembly can overflow prompt budgets and external truncation may cut unrelated system/user content. The defect crosses the interface from feedback rendering into prompt construction.

ANALYSE: HARD for the stated API contract. Premises: the parameter is documented as a “Hard cap”; the current implementation has an execution path where `len(section) > max_chars_per_model` after the truncation loop; no caller-side invariant in this file forbids small caps. Derivation: for any `max_chars_per_model < len(placeholder)`, the assigned placeholder violates `len(section) <= max_chars_per_model`. Conclusion: CONFIRMED.

RESULT: falsifier not satisfied; the bug remains. Fix break attempt: with `max_chars_per_model=10`, final slice returns at most 10 characters; with `max_chars_per_model=0`, it returns `""`; with `max_chars_per_model=-5`, `max(0, -5)` prevents Python’s negative slicing from returning all-but-last characters and instead returns `""`. The fix enforces the hard cap even for degenerate budgets, at the cost of possibly returning an incomplete marker when the cap is tiny; that is unavoidable under a true hard cap.
